subject: pharmacology
title: Antiepileptics and status epilepticus

steps.tx: **Antiepileptics** sort by channel: **sodium blockade** (phenytoin, carbamazepine, lamotrigine, lacosamide; use dependent, partial and tonic clonic), **calcium T blockade** (**ethosuximide** absence), **GABA enhancement** (benzodiazepines, phenobarbital, vigabatrin irreversible, tiagabine reuptake), **glutamate blockade** (topiramate, perampanel AMPA), **SV2A** (**levetiracetam** broad, safe pregnancy). Choice follows seizure type (absence needs ethosuximide or valproate, never phenytoin), age, pregnancy and comorbidity; monotherapy titrates first.
steps.say: Partial and tonic clonic take sodium blockers; absence takes ethosuximide. Never phenytoin absence: worsens.

vis.alt: Sodium blockade with phenytoin, carbamazepine, lamotrigine and lacosamide for partial and tonic-clonic seizures; T-type calcium blockade with ethosuximide for absence; GABA enhancement with benzodiazepines, phenobarbital, vigabatrin and tiagabine; status ladder lorazepam then fosphenytoin, levetiracetam or valproate then midazolam or propofol.
vis.caption: Match the channel to the seizure type; sodium blockers worsen absence.

steps.tx: **Phenytoin** (**zero order** saturation kinetics, **gingival hyperplasia** with hirsutism and megaloblastic anaemia, **HLA-B*1502** hypersensitivity, teratogenic, inducer) needs level monitoring (free in hypoalbuminaemia and renal failure); **carbamazepine** (**autoinduction**, **SIADH hyponatraemia**, agranulocytosis, SJS HLA screened, trigeminal neuralgia first line) interacts widely. **Valproate** (broadest including myoclonus, **neural tube defects** with PCOS, weight gain, pancreatitis, hyperammonaemia, tremor) is avoided in pregnancy; levels with LFTs watch all three.
steps.say: Saturation kinetics, gum overgrowth, HLA rash: phenytoin, watch levels. Autoinduction plus low sodium: carbamazepine.

steps.tx: **Absence** (3 Hz spike wave, hyperventilation provokes, ethosuximide first) and **myoclonic** (valproate or levetiracetam, photosensitive juvenile) epilepsies start young; new agents fill niches (**levetiracetam** irritability, brivaracetam calmer, lacosamide PR prolonging, perampanel aggression, topiramate weight loss with stones and glaucoma, zonisamide sulfa stones, gabapentinoids pain not epilepsy). **Never withdraw abruptly** (rebound status); switch overlapping. Comorbidity guides (migraine topiramate, pain gabapentin, mood valproate or lamotrigine).
steps.say: Blank staring hyperventilated is absence: ethosuximide. Never stop suddenly: status rebounds.

steps.tx: **Status epilepticus** (over 5 minutes convulsive, time is brain) runs **lorazepam IV** (buccal midazolam prehospital, rectal diazepam children) then **fosphenytoin, levetiracetam or valproate** infusion, then **midazolam or propofol** anaesthesia with EEG burst suppression for refractory; pyridoxine in neonates, glucose with thiamine always. Nonconvulsive (prolonged postictal, subtle twitches) needs EEG. **Pregnancy** prefers **levetiracetam or lamotrigine** with high dose folate; breastfeeding mostly continues.
steps.say: Seizing past 5 minutes is status: lorazepam, then fosphenytoin or levetiracetam, then anaesthesia. Pregnant epilepsy prefers levetiracetam.
